name: Carpenter starter feed
note: Copy this file, add your own projects, and point Carpenter at the raw URL from Settings → Project feeds. Sizes are millimetres. stock is board, panel or dowel; a dowel part uses d for diameter instead of t and w.

projects.title: Two-step kitchen stool
projects.blurb: A stool short enough to live under a counter and strong enough to stand on with a full kettle.
steps: Cut both sides together so the tread notches line up exactly.
Glue and screw the treads between the sides, checking for square each time.
Add the back brace last — it is what stops the stool racking sideways.
Round the front edge of each tread so bare feet are happy.
Stand on it hard before anyone else does.
projects.finish: Two coats of matte varnish; skip oil, it stays slippery.
projects.safety: Treads must be dead level. A stool that rocks is a stool that throws you.

projects.title: Hardwood domino set
projects.blurb: Twenty-eight tiles from one strip of hardwood, with drilled and filled pips.

hardwareList.name: Black epoxy or wax crayon for pips

steps: Mill the strips to a consistent 10 × 25 mm before cutting any tiles.
Crosscut 28 tiles at 50 mm using a stop block so they are identical.
Mark the centre line on every tile with a marking gauge.
Drill the pips 3 mm deep with a 4 mm bit, using a paper template.
Fill the pips with black wax or epoxy, then sand the faces flat.
Build the box to fit the finished stack, not to a drawing.
projects.finish: Wax only — tiles need to slide.
projects.safety: Small tiles near a spinning blade need a push stick and a stop block, never fingers.
